06-caltrans-d2.subject: Re: Public Records Act request - Caltrans District 2 roadside vegetation-control (herbicide) records, Plumas / Lassen / Sierra
06-caltrans-d2.body:
Dear Ms. LeBaron and the Caltrans District 2 Public Records staff,

I am following up on the Public Records Act request I emailed to this address on September 13, 2026 for District 2 roadside vegetation-control (herbicide) records on state highways in Plumas, Lassen and Sierra counties, January 1, 2020 to the present: application records by date, route and postmile; the District's annual vegetation-control and herbicide-use reports and Pesticide Use Reports; and any pest-management plan, no-spray lists or public-notification records.

Thank you for your September 14 reply pointing us to the Caltrans public-records portal. We have not received a portal acknowledgement, a reference number, or a determination on this request. Under Government Code section 7922.535, a determination was due within 10 days of receipt, by September 23, 2026.

Could you please either (1) confirm that this email request has been logged and give us its reference number and an estimated production date, or (2) if the request must be entered in the portal before District 2 can act on it, let me know and I will file it there right away, referencing the September 13 date of this email? The application records by route and postmile remain our highest priority, and we are glad to receive them first with the rest to follow.

Electronic delivery is preferred. Thank you for your help.

Sincerely,

Plumas Grassroots Collective / SprayMap California
spraymapca@gmail.com - spraymapca.org

15-reply-laura-boles.subject: Re: SprayMap California — get involved
15-reply-laura-boles.body:
Hi Laura,

No apology needed, and thank you for laying all of this out. Knowing it is Marin, and that your concern is open space and parkland rather than farmland, makes the picture much clearer.

A few starting points, from what we have learned doing this in Plumas County:

1. A records request can be a short email. Under the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code section 7920.000 et seq.), you can write to each local or state agency and ask for its pesticide and herbicide application records for a date range: date, location, product, active ingredient, amount, and area treated, plus any integrated pest management plan or annual pesticide-use report. The agency has 10 days to tell you whether it has responsive records (Gov. Code section 7922.535). You do not have to know in advance where spraying happened. Asking for every application across all of its lands, by date, avoids having to search area by area.

2. Marin County Parks / Open Space, any municipal water district, and California State Parks are all covered by the Public Records Act. Many agencies also have a public-records portal or a named records contact on their website.

3. Golden Gate National Recreation Area, Muir Woods and Point Reyes are National Park Service units, so those requests go under the federal Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) rather than the state Act. Federal agencies have their own FOIA offices and timelines.

4. California's statewide Pesticide Use Report data comes from county agricultural commissioners. As we said before, the newest year on our map is 2023, and much non-agricultural use is reported only as monthly totals, without locations. That is why going straight to the land-managing agencies is often the better route for open space.

If it would help, we are glad to share the wording we have used in our own requests so you can adapt it rather than start from scratch.

Thank you for your kind words, and for doing this work in Marin.

Warmly,

Plumas Grassroots Collective / SprayMap California
spraymapca@gmail.com - spraymapca.org

17-reply-cora-miller.subject: Re: Add me to the SprayMap network
17-reply-cora-miller.body:
Hi Cora,

Thank you for signing up, and for telling us about your dissertation. Fire recovery and land management in Plumas County is very close to what many people in our collective care about.

We would be glad to learn more. Could you send a short description of the project, and what taking part in an interview or having you observe a meeting would involve (time commitment, how information is used and kept confidential, and any consent materials)? That will make it easy to share with members, who can decide for themselves whether to take part.

Thank you again for reaching out.

Warmly,

Plumas Grassroots Collective / SprayMap California
spraymapca@gmail.com - spraymapca.org
